title: Socio-environmental assessment of Aedes aegypti distribution and risk of chikungunya in vulnerable community.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, poses a major public health challenge in tropical regions. In Brazil, its incidence has increased, especially in socioeconomically vulnerable areas, where environmental conditions favor the proliferation of vectors. Our objective was to assess the socioeconomic and environmental vulnerabilities associated with the spatial distribution of a) Ae. aegypti and b) resident exposure to CHIKV in a low-income community. Identifying key exposure hotspots, our work improves our understanding of CHIKV transmission in informal settlements and facilitates community-based interventions to mitigate CHIKV risk. aegypti using ovitraps and conducted a serological survey from October 2021 to June 2022 in a vulnerable informal community in Salvador, Brazil. Blood samples and sociodemographic, household, and environmental data were collected from residents aged ≥5 years. CHIKV serology was performed, and spatial models using Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation assessed vector distribution, seropositivity, and associated factors. Our high-resolution study identified fine-scale vulnerabilities linked to both Ae. aegypti abundance and heightened risk of CHIKV transmission. Based on our findings, effective control strategies should not only focus on traditional methods such as enhancing basic urban infrastructure and services and promoting community awareness, but also target specific breeding sites around homes, address garbage accumulation, and consider the influence of micro-scale temperature variations. These results emphasize the importance of tailored, neighborhood-specific interventions to effectively reduce chikungunya transmission in high-risk communities.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们的目标是评估与Aedes aegypti空间分布以及居民基孔肯雅热暴露相关的社会经济和环境脆弱性,在巴西萨尔瓦多的一个低收入社区中进行。

elements_zh.main_results: 我们的高分辨率研究识别了与埃及伊蚊数量和基孔肯雅热传播风险相关的微尺度脆弱性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 通过识别关键暴露热点,我们的工作提高了我们对基孔肯雅热在非正式聚居区传播机制的理解,并有助于制定基于社区的干预措施以减轻基孔肯雅热风险。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果强调了针对高风险社区制定特定于社区的干预措施的重要性,以有效减少基孔肯雅热的传播。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其仅关注单一社区,可能无法推广到其他环境。此外,使用血清学数据可能无法完全捕捉近期感染情况,且本研究未包括基孔肯雅病毒的分子检测。

abstract_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)通过埃及伊蚊传播,在热带地区构成重大的公共卫生挑战。在巴西,其传播范围不断扩大,尤其是在社会经济脆弱地区,环境条件有利于媒介的繁殖。我们的目标是评估与Aedes aegypti空间分布以及居民基孔肯雅热暴露相关的社会经济和环境脆弱性。通过识别关键暴露热点,我们的工作提高了我们对基孔肯雅热在非正式聚居区传播机制的理解,并有助于制定基于社区的干预措施以减轻基孔肯雅热风险。在巴西萨尔瓦多的一个易感非正式社区中,使用卵笼捕捉埃及伊蚊,并于2021年10月至2022年6月期间对年龄≥5岁的居民进行了血清学调查。收集了居民的血液样本以及社会人口学、家庭和环境数据。进行了基孔肯雅病毒的血清学检测,并使用集成嵌套拉普拉斯近似法(Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation)的空间模型评估了媒介的分布、血清阳性率及相关因素。我们的高分辨率研究识别了与埃及伊蚊数量和基孔肯雅热传播风险相关的微尺度脆弱性。基于我们的研究结果,有效的控制策略不仅应关注传统的增强基本城市基础设施和服务以及促进社区意识的方法,还应针对家庭周围的特定繁殖场所,解决垃圾堆积问题,并考虑微尺度温度变化的影响。这些结果强调了针对高风险社区制定特定于社区的干预措施的重要性,以有效减少基孔肯雅热的传播。

title: Effect of long-term storage on the morphology and infectivity of purified Chikungunya virus
abstract: Abstract Purification and long-term preservation of viral particles are critical steps in virology research, as they directly influence the reliability of structural studies and functional assays supporting vaccine and therapeutic development. Many of these applications, particularly cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and biophysical analyses, require cryoprotectant-free (CPA-free) viral preparations, yet preserving both infectivity and structural integrity under such conditions is especially challenging for enveloped viruses. Here, we describe and validate a practical methodology for purifying and preserving infectious Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) particles for applications in which cryoprotectants cannot be used. CHIKV particles produced in Vero cells were purified by polyethylene glycol (PEG) precipitation followed by discontinuous cesium chloride (CsCl) gradient ultracentrifugation, yielding highly purified preparations with a 70.4% recovery rate and preserved virion morphology, as confirmed by SDS-PAGE, RT-qPCR and negative-staining transmission electron microscopy (TEM). To determine whether freezing rate and ultra-low storage temperature affect long-term preservation, purified CHIKV was subjected to three CPA-free freezing/storage protocols: fast freezing and storage in liquid nitrogen, fast freezing followed by storage at -80°C, and controlled slow freezing followed by storage at -80°C. Infectivity was monitored by plaque assay for up to 202 days post-freezing. Although infectivity declined progressively, no significant differences were observed among the protocols tested, indicating that controlled slow freezing at -80°C is a practical and cost-effective alternative to liquid nitrogen storage. TEM showed preservation of the overall virion morphology under all storage conditions despite the reduced infectivity, suggesting that subtle structural alterations may escape detection by conventional electron microscopy.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenge of preserving the infectivity and structural integrity of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) particles without the use of cryoprotectants, which are critical for reliable structural studies and functional assays in vaccine and therapeutic development.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved purifying CHIKV particles from Vero cells and subjecting them to three CPA-free freezing/storage protocols to evaluate their long-term preservation under different conditions.
analysis.methods: CHIKV particles were purified using polyethylene glycol (PEG) precipitation and discontinuous cesium chloride (CsCl) gradient ultracentrifugation. Infectivity was assessed using plaque assay, and virion morphology was evaluated by negative-staining transmission electron microscopy (TEM).
analysis.main_results: Purified CHIKV particles showed a 70.4% recovery rate and preserved virion morphology across all storage conditions. However, infectivity declined progressively over time, with no significant differences observed among the tested protocols.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that controlled slow freezing at -80°C is a practical and cost-effective alternative to liquid nitrogen storage for preserving CHIKV infectivity without cryoprotectants, as no significant differences in preservation were found among the protocols.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a reliable method for preserving CHIKV particles for structural and functional studies, which can support vaccine and therapeutic development without the need for cryoprotectants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to abstract-only evidence, and the results were based on a single protocol comparison. The evidence is moderate, as the findings are based on observed infectivity decline and morphology preservation without long-term follow-up or additional validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of freezing rate and ultra-low storage temperature on the preservation of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infectivity and morphology without cryoprotectants. The authors developed a methodology involving polyethylene glycol (PEG) precipitation and discontinuous cesium chloride (CsCl) gradient ultracentrifugation to purify CHIKV particles. They tested three freezing/storage protocols: fast freezing and storage in liquid nitrogen, fast freezing followed by storage at -80°C, and controlled slow freezing followed by storage at -80°C. The results showed that infectivity declined progressively over time, but no significant differences were observed among the protocols. The authors concluded that controlled slow freezing at -80°C is a practical and cost-effective alternative to liquid nitrogen storage for preserving CHIKV. The study's findings have implications for virology research, particularly in vaccine and therapeutic development, by offering a method that avoids the use of cryoprotectants. However, the evidence is based solely on abstract information, which limits its strength.

elements_en.methods: CHIKV particles were purified using polyethylene glycol (PEG) precipitation and discontinuous cesium chloride (CsCl) gradient ultracentrifugation. Infectivity was assessed using plaque assay, and virion morphology was evaluated by negative-staining transmission electron microscopy (TEM).
elements_en.main_results: Purified CHIKV particles showed a 70.4% recovery rate and preserved virion morphology across all storage conditions. However, infectivity declined progressively over time, with no significant differences observed among the tested protocols.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that controlled slow freezing at -80°C is a practical and cost-effective alternative to liquid nitrogen storage for preserving CHIKV infectivity without cryoprotectants, as no significant differences in preservation were found among the protocols.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a reliable method for preserving CHIKV particles for structural and functional studies, which can support vaccine and therapeutic development without the need for cryoprotectants.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to abstract-only evidence, and the results were based on a single protocol comparison. The evidence is moderate, as the findings are based on observed infectivity decline and morphology preservation without long-term follow-up or additional validation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在解决在不使用冷冻保护剂的情况下保持基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)颗粒的感染力和结构完整性的挑战,因为冷冻保护剂对于支持疫苗和治疗开发的可靠结构研究和功能实验至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及从Vero细胞中纯化CHIKV颗粒,并将其置于三种无冷冻保护剂的冷冻/储存方案中,以评估其在不同条件下的长期保存效果。
elements_zh.methods: CHIKV颗粒通过聚乙二醇(PEG)沉淀和不连续铯氯化物(CsCl)梯度超速离心进行纯化。感染力通过斑块实验进行评估,病毒颗粒形态则通过负染色传播电子显微镜(TEM)进行分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 纯化的CHIKV颗粒在所有储存条件下均表现出70.4%的回收率,并且病毒颗粒形态得以保留。然而,感染力随时间逐渐下降,且在所测试的方案中未观察到显著差异。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,在-80°C下进行控制缓慢冷冻是一种实用且成本效益高的替代液氮储存方法,用于在不使用冷冻保护剂的情况下保存CHIKV感染力,因为在所测试的方案中未发现保存效果的显著差异。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为在不使用冷冻保护剂的情况下保存CHIKV颗粒提供了可靠的方法,从而支持了结构和功能研究,进而有助于疫苗和治疗开发。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅基于摘要证据,且结果基于单一方案的比较。证据强度中等,因为这些发现基于观察到的感染力下降和形态保存,而没有长期随访或额外验证。

title_zh: 长期储存对纯化基孔肯雅病毒形态和感染力的影响
source_body_en: Abstract Purification and long-term preservation of viral particles are critical steps in virology research, as they directly influence the reliability of structural studies and functional assays supporting vaccine and therapeutic development. Many of these applications, particularly cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and biophysical analyses, require cryoprotectant-free (CPA-free) viral preparations, yet preserving both infectivity and structural integrity under such conditions is especially challenging for enveloped viruses. Here, we describe and validate a practical methodology for purifying and preserving infectious Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) particles for applications in which cryoprotectants cannot be used. CHIKV particles produced in Vero cells were purified by polyethylene glycol (PEG) precipitation followed by discontinuous cesium chloride (CsCl) gradient ultracentrifugation, yielding highly purified preparations with a 70.4% recovery rate and preserved virion morphology, as confirmed by SDS-PAGE, RT-qPCR and negative-staining transmission electron microscopy (TEM). To determine whether freezing rate and ultra-low storage temperature affect long-term preservation, purified CHIKV was subjected to three CPA-free freezing/storage protocols: fast freezing and storage in liquid nitrogen, fast freezing followed by storage at -80°C, and controlled slow freezing followed by storage at -80°C. Infectivity was monitored by plaque assay for up to 202 days post-freezing. Although infectivity declined progressively, no significant differences were observed among the protocols tested, indicating that controlled slow freezing at -80°C is a practical and cost-effective alternative to liquid nitrogen storage. TEM showed preservation of the overall virion morphology under all storage conditions despite the reduced infectivity, suggesting that subtle structural alterations may escape detection by conventional electron microscopy.
abstract_zh: 摘要 病毒颗粒的纯化和长期保存是病毒学研究中的关键步骤,因为它们直接影响支持疫苗和治疗开发的结构研究和功能实验的可靠性。许多这些应用,特别是冷冻电子显微镜(cryo-EM)和生物物理分析,需要无冷冻保护剂(CPA-free)的病毒制备,但在这种条件下保持感染力和结构完整性对包膜病毒来说尤为具有挑战性。在这里,我们描述并验证了一种实用的方法,用于纯化和保存不使用冷冻保护剂的感染性基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)颗粒。从Vero细胞中生产的CHIKV颗粒通过聚乙二醇(PEG)沉淀和不连续铯氯化物(CsCl)梯度超速离心进行纯化,获得了高纯度的制备,回收率为70.4%,并且病毒颗粒形态得以保留,这通过SDS-PAGE、RT-qPCR和负染色传播电子显微镜(TEM)确认。为了确定冷冻速率和超低温储存条件对长期保存的影响,纯化的CHIKV被置于三种无冷冻保护剂的冷冻/储存方案中:快速冷冻并储存在液氮中、快速冷冻后储存在-80°C、以及控制缓慢冷冻后储存在-80°C。感染力通过冻后202天内的斑块实验进行监测。尽管感染力随时间逐渐下降,但在所测试的方案中未观察到显著差异,这表明在-80°C下进行控制缓慢冷冻是一种实用且成本效益高的替代液氮储存的方法。TEM显示在所有储存条件下病毒颗粒的整体形态均得以保留,尽管感染力有所下降,这表明细微的结构变化可能无法通过常规电子显微镜检测到。

title: Chikungunya Awareness and Related Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Among Nursing Students at the University of Palermo, Italy: A Cross-Sectional Study of Associated Sociodemographic Factors
abstract: Introduction: Chikungunya is an emerging mosquito-borne viral disease that has become a growing public health concern worldwide. Despite documented autochthonous outbreaks in Italy and the increasing spread of Aedes albopictus mosquitoes across Europe, little is known about awareness of chikungunya among future healthcare professionals. This study aimed to assess awareness of chikungunya and evaluate related knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAPs) among nursing students at the University of Palermo, Italy. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted in May 2026 among undergraduate nursing students enrolled at the University of Palermo. Data were collected through an anonymous self-administered online questionnaire investigating sociodemographic characteristics, awareness of chikungunya, sources of information, and KAP related to the disease. Associations between awareness and participant characteristics were assessed using chi-square tests and prevalence ratio analyses. Results: A total of 894 students participated (mean age: 22.33 ± 4.53 years; 72.3% female). Overall, only 22 students (2.46%) reported having previously heard of chikungunya. In a multivariable exploratory analysis, third-year students had a higher prevalence of previous awareness compared with first-year students (PR = 3.38; 95% CI: 1.10–10.36), whereas no statistically significant association was observed for age (PR = 1.07; 95% CI: 1.00–1.15). Mass media represented the main source of information (63.6%), followed by university lectures (22.7%). Among participants who reported previous awareness, responses suggested relatively good recognition of major clinical manifestations, although important gaps were observed regarding vector recognition and transmission pathways. Attitudes toward prevention were predominantly positive, and most participants reported adopting recommended mosquito-control practices. Conclusions: Awareness of chikungunya among nursing students was extremely low. Strengthening educational interventions on emerging vector-borne diseases within nursing curricula may improve preparedness, risk communication, and future public health responses.

abstract_zh: 引言:基孔肯雅热是一种新兴的蚊媒病毒性疾病,已成为全球日益严重的公共卫生问题。尽管在意大利已记录到本地传播的基孔肯雅病毒,且欧洲范围内白纹伊蚊的传播范围不断扩大,但关于未来医疗专业人员对基孔肯雅热的认知仍知之甚少。本研究旨在评估护理专业学生对基孔肯雅热的认知,并评估其相关知识、态度和行为(KAPs)。方法:2026年5月,在意大利帕勒莫大学进行了一项横断面研究,调查在读护理专业本科生。通过匿名的自我管理在线问卷收集数据,内容涉及社会人口学特征、基孔肯雅热的认知、信息来源以及与该疾病相关的KAP。使用卡方检验和比值比分析评估认知与参与者特征之间的关联。结果:共有894名学生参与(平均年龄:22.33 ± 4.53岁;72.3%为女性)。总体而言,仅有22名学生(2.46%)表示之前听说过基孔肯雅热。在多变量探索性分析中,第三年学生比第一年学生有更高的基孔肯雅热认知比值比(PR = 3.38;95% CI:1.10–10.36),而年龄与认知之间未观察到统计学显著关联(PR = 1.07;95% CI:1.00–1.15)。大众媒体是主要的信息来源(63.6%),其次是大学课程(22.7%)。在报告过基孔肯雅热认知的参与者中,其对主要临床表现的识别相对较好,但关于基孔肯雅病毒传播途径的识别仍存在重要差距。参与者对预防的态度总体积极,大多数参与者报告采用了推荐的蚊虫控制措施。结论:护理专业学生对基孔肯雅热的认知极低。在护理课程中加强关于新兴蚊媒病毒的教育干预,可能有助于提高应对能力、风险沟通能力和未来的公共卫生响应水平。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 基孔肯雅热是一种新兴的蚊媒病毒性疾病,已成为全球日益严重的公共卫生问题。尽管在意大利已记录到本地传播的基孔肯雅病毒,且欧洲范围内白纹伊蚊的传播范围不断扩大,但关于未来医疗专业人员对基孔肯雅热的认知仍知之甚少。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 2026 年 5 月,对巴勒莫大学注册的护理本科生进行了一项横断面研究。共有 894 名学生参与(平均年龄:22.33 ± 4.53 岁;72.3% 为女性)。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过匿名自填在线调查问卷收集数据,调查社会人口学特征、基孔肯雅热认知度、信息来源以及与该疾病相关的 KAP。使用卡方检验和 患病率 比率分析来评估意识和参与者特征之间的关联。
analysis_zh.main_results: 总体而言,只有 22 名学生 (2.46%) 表示以前听说过基孔肯雅热。在多变量探索性分析中,与一年级学生相比,三年级学生的 患病率 先前认知度更高(PR = 3.38;95% CI:1.10–10.36),而与年龄没有观察到统计学上显着的关联(PR = 1.07;95% CI:1.00–1.15)。大众媒体是主要的信息来源(63.6%),其次是大学讲座(22.7%)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 护生对基孔肯雅热的认知度极低。在报告先前意识的参与者中,反应表明对主要临床表现的识别相对较好,尽管在 媒介 识别和 传播 通路方面观察到重要差距。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 在护理课程中加强对新出现的 媒介 传播疾病的教育干预可能会改善准备情况、风险沟通和未来的公共卫生应对措施。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告本研究的局限性。

title: Alphavirus Nsp3 protein hijacks receptor-mediated mitophagy via BNIP3L/NIX to dampen IFN response and promote viral replication
abstract: Alphaviruses encompass a variety of human and animal pathogens, such as getah virus (GETV), chikungunya virus (CHIKV), and Sindbis virus (SINV). Increasing evidence suggests that innate immunity plays an important role in host resistance to alphavirus infection, while alphaviruses have evolved multiple strategies to evade host antiviral innate immunity. Mitochondria, as key immune hubs, play a central role in the initiation of innate antiviral responses. It remains unclear whether alphaviruses inhibit innate immune responses by manipulating mitochondria. In this study, we found that GETV infection damages mitochondrial structure and function, as shown by mitochondrial membrane potential depolarization, reduction in mitochondrial numbers, and an imbalance in mitochondrial dynamics. GETV infection induces mitophagy in host cells and promotes viral replication. Nsp3 protein of alphaviruses (CHIKV, SINV, GETV) can directly trigger receptor-mediated mitophagy through its interaction with BNIP3L/NIX. Knockdown of BNIP3L could alleviate mitophagy caused by GETV infection. Mitophagy induced by alphavirus Nsp3 protein leads to degradation of MAVS which inhibits the IFN response and promotes viral replication. Collectively, our results demonstrated that alphaviruses Nsp3 serves as a novel virulence factor, inducing BNIP3L-mediated mitophagy to degrade MAVS and evade the host immune response.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate whether alphaviruses inhibit innate immune responses by manipulating mitochondria, as it remains unclear how these viruses interact with host immune mechanisms.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on alphaviruses, specifically Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), and examined their effects on host cell mitochondria and immune responses in vitro and in vivo.
analysis.methods: The researchers used molecular and cellular techniques to assess mitochondrial structure and function, including measuring mitochondrial membrane potential, mitochondrial numbers, and dynamics. They also evaluated mitophagy and its impact on MAVS degradation and IFN response.
analysis.main_results: The study found that CHIKV infection damages mitochondrial structure and function, as evidenced by mitochondrial membrane potential depolarization, reduction in mitochondrial numbers, and an imbalance in mitochondrial dynamics. Additionally, CHIKV infection induces mitophagy, which promotes viral replication.

title_zh: 甲病毒 Nsp3 蛋白通过 BNIP3L/NIX 劫持受体介导的线粒体自噬,抑制 IFN 反应并促进病毒复制
source_body_en: Alphaviruses encompass a variety of human and animal pathogens, such as getah virus (GETV), chikungunya virus (CHIKV), and Sindbis virus (SINV). Increasing evidence suggests that innate immunity plays an important role in host resistance to alphavirus infection, while alphaviruses have evolved multiple strategies to evade host antiviral innate immunity. Mitochondria, as key immune hubs, play a central role in the initiation of innate antiviral responses. It remains unclear whether alphaviruses inhibit innate immune responses by manipulating mitochondria. In this study, we found that GETV infection damages mitochondrial structure and function, as shown by mitochondrial membrane potential depolarization, reduction in mitochondrial numbers, and an imbalance in mitochondrial dynamics. GETV infection induces mitophagy in host cells and promotes viral replication. Nsp3 protein of alphaviruses (CHIKV, SINV, GETV) can directly trigger receptor-mediated mitophagy through its interaction with BNIP3L/NIX. Knockdown of BNIP3L could alleviate mitophagy caused by GETV infection. Mitophagy induced by alphavirus Nsp3 protein leads to degradation of MAVS which inhibits the IFN response and promotes viral replication. Collectively, our results demonstrated that alphaviruses Nsp3 serves as a novel virulence factor, inducing BNIP3L-mediated mitophagy to degrade MAVS and evade the host immune response.

title: COINFECTION WITH PLASMODIUM VIVAX AND CHIKUNGUNYA; WHEN FEBRILE ILLNESS EVOLVES INTO HYPERDYNAMIC SHOCK: CASE REPORT
abstract: Coinfection with malaria and chikungunya is a rare presentation and poses a diagnostic challenge., especially since both infections can produce systemic manifestations and hemodynamic compromise. We present the case of a 23-year-old female patient from an urban area with no known past medical history, who presented with a seven-day history of fever, dizziness, generalized weakness, arthralgia, and vomiting. On admission, she was febrile, tachycardic, and hypotensive, with an insufficient hemodynamic response to initial resuscitation with crystalloids, requiring vasopressor support. Advanced cardiovascular evaluation revealed a predominantly vasodilatory and hyperdynamic profile, characterized by high cardiac output, decreased systemic vascular resistance, and preserved stroke volume. Left and right ventricular systolic and diastolic function remained preserved, with adequate TAPSE and MAPSE, and no significant chamber dilation or regional contractility abnormalities. The electrocardiogram and cardiac enzymes showed no evidence of myocardial injury or myocarditis. Studies revealed severe anemia, with a hemoglobin level of 6 g/ dL, and hepatosplenomegaly. Thick blood smear identified Plasmodium. The patient tested positive for vivax, while the PCR test for chikungunya was positive and the dengue test was negative, confirming the coinfection. Intravenous artesunate was initiated, followed by artemether-lumefantrine, in addition to vasoactive support and transfusion of two units of packed red blood cells. The patient experienced progressive hemodynamic recovery and a favorable clinical course. This case highlights the importance of considering vector-borne coinfections and characterizing the hemodynamic phenotype to differentiate vasodilatory shock from cardiogenic compromise.
journal: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews

title_zh: 间日疟原虫和基孔肯雅热混合感染;当发热性疾病演变为高动力休克时:病例报告
source_body_en: Coinfection with malaria and chikungunya is a rare presentation and poses a diagnostic challenge., especially since both infections can produce systemic manifestations and hemodynamic compromise. We present the case of a 23-year-old female patient from an urban area with no known past medical history, who presented with a seven-day history of fever, dizziness, generalized weakness, arthralgia, and vomiting. On admission, she was febrile, tachycardic, and hypotensive, with an insufficient hemodynamic response to initial resuscitation with crystalloids, requiring vasopressor support. Advanced cardiovascular evaluation revealed a predominantly vasodilatory and hyperdynamic profile, characterized by high cardiac output, decreased systemic vascular resistance, and preserved stroke volume. Left and right ventricular systolic and diastolic function remained preserved, with adequate TAPSE and MAPSE, and no significant chamber dilation or regional contractility abnormalities. The electrocardiogram and cardiac enzymes showed no evidence of myocardial injury or myocarditis. Studies revealed severe anemia, with a hemoglobin level of 6 g/ dL, and hepatosplenomegaly. Thick blood smear identified Plasmodium. The patient tested positive for vivax, while the PCR test for chikungunya was positive and the dengue test was negative, confirming the coinfection. Intravenous artesunate was initiated, followed by artemether-lumefantrine, in addition to vasoactive support and transfusion of two units of packed red blood cells. The patient experienced progressive hemodynamic recovery and a favorable clinical course. This case highlights the importance of considering vector-borne coinfections and characterizing the hemodynamic phenotype to differentiate vasodilatory shock from cardiogenic compromise.
abstract_zh: 疟疾和基孔肯雅热的混合感染是一种罕见的表现,对诊断提出了挑战,特别是因为两种感染都会产生全身表现和血流动力学损害。我们介绍了一名来自城市地区的 23 岁女性患者,无既往病史,有 7 天发热、头晕、全身无力、关节痛 和呕吐病史。入院时,她出现发热、心动过速和低血压,对晶体液初始复苏的血流动力学反应不足,需要血管加压药支持。高级心血管评估显示主要是血管舒张和高动力特征,其特征是高心输出量、降低的全身血管阻力和保留的每搏输出量。左心室和右心室收缩和舒张功能仍然保留,具有足够的 TAPSE 和 MAPSE,并且没有明显的心室扩张或局部收缩力异常。心电图和心肌酶显示没有心肌损伤或心肌炎的证据。研究显示严重贫血,血红蛋白水平为 6 g/dL,并且肝脾肿大。厚厚的血涂片鉴定出疟原虫。该患者的间日疟检测呈阳性,而基孔肯雅热PCR检测呈阳性,登革热检测呈阴性,证实了双重感染。开始静脉注射青蒿琥酯,随后使用蒿甲醚-本芴醇,此外还进行血管活性支持和输注两个单位的浓缩红细胞。患者的血流动力学逐渐恢复,临床病程良好。该病例强调了考虑 媒介 传播的合并感染和表征血流动力学表型以区分血管舒张性休克和心源性损害的重要性。

title: Antiviral Sulfonated Polymersomes Inhibit Corona-, Influenza-, and Alphavirus
abstract: A broad-spectrum antiviral is required to enable rapid intervention against current, newly emerging and mutating viruses. Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), influenza A virus (IAV), Sindbis virus (SINV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) all engage negatively charged moieties on host cells, such as heparan sulfate (HS) and sialic acid, to facilitate attachment for entry and infection. We designed HS-mimetic nanoparticles in the form of polymer vesicles (polymersomes) by blending membrane-forming and sulfonated copolymers. These biocompatible polymersomes successfully inhibited host cell infection of HS-dependent SARS-CoV-2 and HS-independent IAV in vitro with sub-nanomolar potency. Multivalent interaction of several virus ligands with a single polymersome as quantified by fluorescence correlation spectroscopy likely contributes to their potency. The sulfonated polymersomes also functioned in vivo as demonstrated by a reduction in the spread of SINV, an alphavirus model for CHIKV, in zebrafish embryos, which led to a significantly increased survival. Hence, our polymersomes could form the basis for an urgently required multifunctional broad-spectrum antiviral nanomedicine.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a broad-spectrum antiviral to address the challenges posed by current and emerging viruses. The researchers designed HS-mimetic polymer vesicles (polymersomes) to target viruses that use negatively charged host cell moieties for entry. The polymersomes showed potent in vitro inhibition of SARS-CoV-2 and IAV, and in vivo efficacy was demonstrated against SINV, a model for CHIKV. The findings suggest that multivalent interactions of virus ligands with polymersomes enhance their antiviral potency. These results highlight the potential of sulfonated polymersomes as a novel nanomedicine for combating multiple viral pathogens. However, the study's conclusions are based on in vitro and in vivo models, and further research is needed to validate these findings in clinical settings.

These biocompatible polymersomes successfully inhibited host cell infection of HS-dependent SARS-CoV-2 and HS-independent IAV in vitro with sub-nanomolar potency. Multivalent interaction of several virus ligands with a single polymersome as quantified by fluorescence correlation spectroscopy likely contributes to their potency. The sulfonated polymersomes also functioned in vivo as demonstrated by a reduction in the spread of SINV, an alphavirus model for CHIKV, in zebrafish embryos, which led to a significantly increased survival. Hence, our polymersomes could form the basis for an urgently required multifunctional broad-spectrum antiviral nanomedicine.

title: Global Genomic Surveillance.
abstract: Global genomic surveillance has emerged as a foundational pillar of public health in the twenty-first century, enabling real-time tracking of pathogen evolution and informing outbreak response. This chapter examines the strategic architecture of global genomic surveillance, focusing on its application to arboviruses such as chikungunya virus (CHIKV). It explores the integration of genomic data with epidemiological, clinical, and environmental information within a One Health framework, while addressing critical challenges in governance, equity, and interoperability. The discussion covers the entire genomic surveillance workflow, from sample collection and sequencing to bioinformatic analysis and phylogenetic inference, and highlights the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) in predictive surveillance. By analyzing global initiatives, operational barriers, and emerging technologies, this chapter underscores the necessity of sustainable, equitable, and interoperable genomic systems to proactively address current and future infectious disease threats.

title: Changes in arbovirus risks and responses from 2020 to 2026
abstract: Abstract Since 2020, viruses spread by mosquitoes and biting midges have become a larger and less predictable public health challenge. Dengue continues to cause the greatest burden, but chikungunya, Oropouche, and other viruses are re-emerging or spreading into new areas. In this narrative review, we summarize major changes in arbovirus epidemiology, surveillance, diagnosis, vaccination, treatment, vector ecology, and mosquito control from 2020 to 2026. New tools can help detect risk earlier and prevent disease, but their usefulness depends on local capacity, safety monitoring, affordability, environmental considerations, and sustained implementation. The next phase of arbovirus control will depend on using these tools strategically, equitably, and before outbreaks overwhelm health systems.

Dengue continues to cause the greatest burden, but chikungunya, Oropouche, and other viruses are re-emerging or spreading into new areas. In this narrative review, we summarize major changes in arbovirus epidemiology, surveillance, diagnosis, vaccination, treatment, vector ecology, and mosquito control from 2020 to 2026. New tools can help detect risk earlier and prevent disease, but their usefulness depends on local capacity, safety monitoring, affordability, environmental considerations, and sustained implementation. The next phase of arbovirus control will depend on using these tools strategically, equitably, and before outbreaks overwhelm health systems.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines changes in arbovirus risks and responses from 2020 to 2026, with a focus on Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and its associated disease manifestations. It highlights the increasing public health challenge posed by CHIKV and other arboviruses, particularly those transmitted by mosquitoes and biting midges. The review summarizes major shifts in epidemiology, surveillance, diagnosis, vaccination, treatment, vector ecology, and mosquito control. It also identifies controversies and evidence gaps related to the implementation of new tools for risk detection and disease prevention. The implications suggest that future arbovirus control efforts must prioritize strategic, equitable, and timely use of these tools to prevent health system overload during outbreaks.

title: Solanaceae-Derived Spirostane Saponins Inhibit Dengue Virus Replication and Viral Protein Expression and Exhibit Activity Against Multiple Arboviruses.
abstract: Mosquito-borne arboviruses, including dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), represent a growing global health burden, yet no specific antiviral therapies are currently available for most of these infections. This unmet need highlights the importance of identifying novel antiviral compounds from biologically relevant sources such as plant-derived natural products. In this study, a bioactivity-guided approach was applied to methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species to identify compounds with antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells. Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Subsequent fractionation and purification led to the isolation of four spirostane-type steroidal saponins, structurally characterized by UPLC-DAD-MS and 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy. Functional assays demonstrated that these compounds inhibit DENV replication, as evidenced by marked reductions in viral RNA levels, NS1 and NS3 protein expression, and infectious viral titers. Stage-specific analyses revealed that their antiviral activity is primarily associated with intracellular phases of the viral life cycle, consistent with inhibition of viral replication and/or protein processing. Molecular docking analyses supported these findings by predicting favorable interactions with key viral enzymes, particularly NS5 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and NS3 helicase/protease. Importantly, the isolated compounds retained antiviral activity against ZIKV and CHIKV, indicating cross-arboviral efficacy. Together, these findings identify spirostane saponins as promising antiviral scaffolds and support their further development as broad-spectrum antiviral agents.

This unmet need highlights the importance of identifying novel antiviral compounds from biologically relevant sources such as plant-derived natural products. In this study, a bioactivity-guided approach was applied to methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species to identify compounds with antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells. Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Subsequent fractionation and purification led to the isolation of four spirostane-type steroidal saponins, structurally characterized by UPLC-DAD-MS and 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy. Functional assays demonstrated that these compounds inhibit DENV replication, as evidenced by marked reductions in viral RNA levels, NS1 and NS3 protein expression, and infectious viral titers. Stage-specific analyses revealed that their antiviral activity is primarily associated with intracellular phases of the viral life cycle, consistent with inhibition of viral replication and/or protein processing. Molecular docking analyses supported these findings by predicting favorable interactions with key viral enzymes, particularly NS5 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and NS3 helicase/protease. Importantly, the isolated compounds retained antiviral activity against ZIKV and CHIKV, indicating cross-arboviral efficacy. Together, these findings identify spirostane saponins as promising antiviral scaffolds and support their further development as broad-spectrum antiviral agents.
title_original: Solanaceae-Derived Spirostane Saponins Inhibit Dengue Virus Replication and Viral Protein Expression and Exhibit Activity Against Multiple Arboviruses.

The research highlights the growing global health burden of mosquito-borne viruses, including chikungunya, and the lack of specific therapies. The findings indicate that these compounds could be promising scaffolds for developing broad-spectrum antiviral agents. The results may inform future research into plant-derived therapies for chikungunya and related viruses, contributing to surveillance and treatment strategies.

title_zh: 来自茄科植物的螺甾烷皂苷抑制登革病毒复制和病毒蛋白表达,并对多种虫媒病毒具有活性。

abstract_zh: 由蚊子传播的虫媒病毒,包括登革病毒(DENV)、寨卡病毒(ZIKV)和基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV),构成了日益增长的全球健康负担,但目前针对这些感染的特定抗病毒药物疗法尚不普及。这种未满足的需求凸显了从生物相关来源(如植物来源的天然产物)中识别新型抗病毒药物化合物的重要性。本研究采用生物活性引导的方法,对八种茄科植物的甲醇提取物进行筛选,以鉴定具有抗病毒药物活性的化合物,针对Vero细胞中的DENV-2。五种提取物显著降低了病毒感染性,其中Solanum ovalifolium和Cestrum sp.在非细胞毒性浓度下实现了完全抑制。随后的分级和纯化过程分离出四种螺甾烷型甾体皂苷,其结构通过UPLC-DAD-MS和1D/2D NMR光谱法进行了表征。功能实验表明,这些化合物抑制了DENV的复制,表现为病毒RNA水平的显著降低、NS1和NS3蛋白表达的减少以及传染性病毒滴度的下降。阶段特异性分析显示,其抗病毒药物活性主要与病毒生命周期的细胞内阶段相关,这与抑制病毒复制和/或蛋白加工一致。分子对接分析支持了这些发现,预测了这些化合物与关键病毒酶的有利相互作用,特别是NS5 RNA依赖性RNA聚合酶和NS3解旋酶/蛋白酶。重要的是,分离出的化合物对ZIKV和CHIKV也表现出抗病毒药物活性,表明其对多种虫媒病毒具有交叉疗效。综上所述,这些发现将螺甾烷皂苷识别为有前景的抗病毒药物骨架,并支持其进一步开发为广谱抗病毒药物药物。

title: Laboratory-based trends in dengue and other arboviruses in the Caribbean: Analysis of surveillance data, 2018-2024
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective: To describe laboratory-based patterns of arboviral circulation, including serotype distribution and temporal trends, and their contribution to regional situational awareness in the Caribbean. Methods: This was a retrospective analysis using clinical samples submitted to the Caribbean Public Health Agency Medical Microbiology Laboratory for suspected arboviral infection. Samples were tested using Trioplex real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction and immunoglobulin M and G enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. Data were analyzed by virus type, serotype, age group, sex, and seasonality. Statistical associations were assessed using Pearson’s chi-square tests. Because the dataset is based on submitted samples, findings are presented as proportions among tested samples rather than population-level estimates. Results: Dengue virus (DENV) accounted for the largest proportion of confirmed arboviral infections (34.7%) among tested samples, with DENV-3 as the most frequently detected serotype (65.5%), followed by DENV-2 (26.8%), DENV-1 (4.3%), and DENV-4 (0.17%). Significant associations were observed between serotype and age group (χ2 = 201.88; P < 0.001) and sex (χ2 = 22.15; P = 0.036). Seasonal peaks were observed primarily between August and November, although an atypical increase in early 2024 was noted. Chikungunya (0.2%) and Zika (0.1%) viruses were infrequently detected. Conclusions: In this retrospective analysis, DENV was the most frequently detected arbovirus among tested samples in the Caribbean, with dynamic serotype distribution and marked seasonal variability. title: Molecular Cloning and Reverse Genetics.
abstract: This chapter describes a detailed molecular biology protocol for introducing specific point mutations into the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genome using a reverse genetics strategy. The method utilizes an overlapping PCR-based approach to generate a mutated DNA fragment, which is then cloned into a pre-engineered CHIKV infectious clone plasmid. The protocol covers all major steps, from the initial PCRs to create the mutated insert to its digestion and ligation into the vector. It also includes procedures for bacterial transformation, colony screening via PCR and Sanger sequencing to confirm the mutation, and plasmid purification via miniprep. The document is structured with a clear introduction, a list of all required reagents and equipment, and a step-by-step methods section.

title: Screening of Antiviral Agents Against CHIKV Using Reporter Virus.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) causes a disease characterized by chronic musculoskeletal inflammation for which specific antivirals are not yet available. Currently, a supportive therapy to alleviate fever and pain is used, but it does not limit viral replication or the persistence of chronic arthritis symptoms. Thus, the identification and development of new active molecules against CHIKV is urgently needed. Here, we present a cell-based methodology that enables the implementation of a rapid and cost-effective strategy for high- and medium-throughput screening (HTS) of compounds, including repurposed drugs or novel molecules. This methodology allows for the identification of novel antiviral hits with a good activity and selectivity profile against CHIKV.

source_body_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) causes a disease characterized by chronic musculoskeletal inflammation for which specific antivirals are not yet available. Currently, a supportive therapy to alleviate fever and pain is used, but it does not limit viral replication or the persistence of chronic arthritis symptoms. Thus, the identification and development of new active molecules against CHIKV is urgently needed. Here, we present a cell-based methodology that enables the implementation of a rapid and cost-effective strategy for high- and medium-throughput screening (HTS) of compounds, including repurposed drugs or novel molecules. This methodology allows for the identification of novel antiviral hits with a good activity and selectivity profile against CHIKV.

title: Epitope Tagging and Coimmunoprecipitation to Identify Viral Protein Interactors.
abstract: Affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS) is a powerful proteomic approach for dissecting the interaction network between virus and host. Traditional AP-MS employs overexpression of viral proteins as baits to enrich host interactors. However, overexpressed viral proteins may mislocalize to inappropriate cellular compartments and trigger endoplasmic reticulum stress by overwhelming the protein-folding machinery, which leads to false identification of host factors. To overcome these limitations, we introduce an AP-MS strategy based on direct infection with an epitope-tagged chikungunya virus (CHIKV/myc-E2), which we used to successfully uncover two new antiviral factors in CHIKV cellular reservoirs-macrophages. In this protocol, we will describe this technique step by step: (1) design and construction of myc-tagged virus by advanced multi-fragment assembly, (2) in vitro transcription and preparation of infectious myc-tagged virus stocks, and (3) immunoprecipitation of myc-tagged viral protein and its interactome for mass spectrometry analysis. This strategy enables accurate identification of viral interactors in a physiologically relevant context, providing a framework for future proteomic studies using tagged viruses.

abstract_zh: 亲和纯化质谱 (AP-MS) 是一种强大的蛋白质组学方法,用于剖析病毒和 宿主 之间的相互作用网络。传统的 AP-MS 采用病毒蛋白的过度表达作为诱饵来丰富 宿主 相互作用子。然而,过度表达的病毒蛋白可能会错误定位到不适当的细胞区室,并通过压倒蛋白质折叠机制而引发内质网应激,从而导致 宿主 因子的错误识别。为了克服这些限制,我们引入了一种基于直接感染表位标记的 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV/myc-E2) 的 AP-MS 策略,我们用它成功地发现了 CHIKV 细胞 储存宿主 巨噬细胞中的两个新的 抗病毒药物 因子。在本协议中,我们将逐步描述该技术:(1)通过先进的多片段组装设计和构建 myc 标记病毒,(2)体外转录和制备感染性 myc 标记病毒库存,(3)免疫沉淀 myc 标记病毒蛋白及其相互作用组进行质谱分析。该策略能够在生理相关背景下准确识别病毒相互作用因子,为未来使用标记病毒的蛋白质组学研究提供框架。

title: A Restriction-Free Cloning Approach for Molecular Engineering of Plasmids.
abstract: Molecular cloning by PCR amplification using a highly processive, high-fidelity DNA polymerase represents a robust and versatile technique for the precise manipulation of nucleic acid sequences. This approach enables the insertion, replacement, or modification of specific DNA fragments within a cloning vector, thereby generating an accurate copy of a gene or viral segment for downstream applications, such as protein expression, site-directed mutagenesis, and structural or functional analyses. The use of processive, high-fidelity polymerases significantly reduces the occurrence of base substitution errors, ensuring sequence integrity throughout the amplification process. Traditionally, restriction enzymes have been employed to facilitate directional cloning; however, alternative methods allow for mutagenesis without the need for unique and specific restriction sites and can be applied to virtually any cloning or seamless DNA assembly strategy. In this chapter, we describe a restriction enzyme-free and ligation-free PCR-based protocol widely applicable to any circular vector. This method enables targeted mutagenesis of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genome, offering a fast, efficient, and reliable strategy for generating mutant constructs suitable for virological and molecular studies.

title: Provenance and competence for CHIKV and DENV of Aedes albopictus populations
abstract: Aedes albopictus is one of the world’s most hazardous invasive species, increasingly implicated in the autochthonous transmission of Chikungunya (CHIKV) and Dengue (DENV) viruses in newly colonized areas. Since invading the Mediterranean Basin several in the early 1980s, recurrent introductions of distinct lineages have driven extensive genomic admixture within adventive populations. This study investigates whether and how the complex dynamics of these diverse genetic backgrounds have shaped variations in vector competence for CHIKV, DENV, and Zika (ZIKV) viruses. Using highly polymorphic simple sequence repeat (SSR) markers, we genotyped Ae. Albopictus samples from an ancestral population (Guangzhou, China) and ten adventive populations across five Mediterranean regions (Southern Switzerland, Northern/Central Italy, the Balkans, and Greece). Genetic ancestry and demographic histories were inferred using Bayesian STRUCTURE (v2.3.2.0) and DIYABC-RF. The association between population ancestry and vector competence for CHIKV (06.21), DENV-1, and ZIKV (PE243) was assessed using infection rate, dissemination efficiency, and transmission efficiency indices, analyzed via univariate and multivariate models. Combining historical records with demographic models revealed that the establishment of Ae. Albopictus in the Mediterranean was driven by chaotic, discontinuous lineage introductions and admixture events, resulting in high spatial and ancestry heterogeneity. Notably, this genetic heterogeneity significantly influences vector competence, in particular for CHIKV and DENV. Interestingly, populations in neighboring geographical areas with distinct ancestries exhibited drastically different competence profiles, whereas geographically distant populations sharing genetic ancestry displayed similar vector competence for CHIKV and DENV. Our findings demonstrate that the complex population dynamics and colonization history of Ae. Albopictus contributes to variation in vector competence, altering the geographical landscape of arboviral risk. These results underscore the urgent need for localized, geographically tailored vector control strategies in Europe, a region facing a rising trend of both imported and autochthonous arboviral infections.

title: Analysis of Cell Populations from Arbovirus-Infected Tissues by Flow Cytometry.
abstract: Arboviruses still represent a major challenge to public health in many parts of the world. Despite shared epidemiological characteristics, each arboviral disorder displays distinct cellular tropism and activation patterns, progressing to immunopathological outcomes that remain not fully elucidated. A deeper understanding of these processes requires methodologies capable of characterizing the often-complex cellular responses. In this context, flow cytometry emerges as a valuable tool, enabling the characterization of heterogeneous cell populations, the assessment of activation and proliferation markers, the quantification of inflammatory mediators, and the detection of cell death pathways. By integrating these parameters, flow cytometry can enhance our understanding of arbovirus pathogenesis, clarify their cellular tropism, and understand immune responses to infection. This methodological article outlines the main steps for applying the technique to different target tissues infected by chikungunya, dengue, yellow fever, and Zika viruses, emphasizing the most effective strategies.

title: Vertical oviposition preference of Aedes albopictus (Skuse, 1895) (Diptera: Culicidae) at different heights and seasonal periods in an urban forest fragment in Manaus, Amazonas, Brazil
abstract: Mosquitoes of the genus Aedes Meigen, 1818 (Diptera: Culicidae) are important vectors of several arboviruses, including those that cause dengue, Zika, and chikungunya. Despite their epidemiological relevance, the vertical distribution of these species in large urban centers remains insufficiently documented. This study evaluated the vertical oviposition preference of Aedes albopictus (Skuse, 1895) at different heights during different seasonal periods. The research was conducted in a six-floor tower located within an urban forest fragment in Manaus, Brazil. The tower measured 15.13 m in height and 3.20 m at its base. Sampling was conducted at the following heights: ground level, 1.20 m, 2.50 m, 3.60 m, 4.90 m, 6.00 m, 7.30 m, 8.40 m, 9.70 m, and 10.80 m. Three ovitraps were installed at each height level, spaced 1.50 m apart, totaling 30 ovitraps per sampling. Monitoring was conducted daily over a 10-week period, with five weeks in the dry season and five weeks in the rainy season. The ovitrap positivity index and egg density index were used to compare population patterns among height levels and between seasons. Egg abundance was higher at lower heights. Relative humidity was positively associated with the mean number of eggs, particularly during the dry season. Although most eggs were recorded in the lower strata, their presence at higher levels indicates that Ae. albopictus is able to occupy elevated environments when conditions are suitable. These findings reinforce the need to consider vertical distribution in vector surveillance programs, especially in urban areas undergoing vertical expansion.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估白纹伊蚊在不同季节期的垂直产卵偏好,因为这些蚊子是多种虫媒病毒的重要媒介,包括引起登革热、寨卡病毒和基孔肯雅热的病毒。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究在巴西马瑙斯市一个六层的城市森林碎片中的塔楼内进行,持续时间为10周,其中前5周为旱季,后5周为雨季。每个高度层安装三个卵 trap,总计每个采样设置30个卵 trap。
elements_zh.methods: 使用卵 trap阳性指数和卵密度指数来比较不同高度层和不同季节间的种群模式。采样在特定高度进行,包括地面层、1.20米、2.50米、3.60米、4.90米、6.00米、7.30米、8.40米、9.70米和10.80米。
elements_zh.main_results: 卵的数量在较低高度处更为丰富。相对湿度与卵的平均数量呈正相关,尤其是在旱季期间。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,当条件适宜时,白纹伊蚊能够占据高处环境,强调了在媒介 监测项目中考虑垂直分布的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可以为城市地区,特别是正在经历垂直扩展的地区,提供关于媒介 监测项目的参考,通过强调考虑垂直分布以制定有效的控制策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于对摘要的分析,证据具有普遍性,因此对垂直产卵模式的解释具有中等置信度。

full_text: AbstractChikungunya virus remains a crucial global health issue with no approved therapy available. In particular, the viral replication is associated with the non-structural protein 2 protease (nsP2pro). In this study, possible inhibitors for nsP2pro from the National Cancer Institute (NCI) database were screened via computational approaches. Molecular docking simulations were initially predicted top potential ligands. MD simulations were then performed to refine the ligand binding pose. During the equilibrium intervals, the ligands formed rigid contacts with the residues Asn476, Ala511, Tyr512, Tyr544 and Trp549 of nsP2pro. Moreover, five compounds probably prevent the biological activity of nsP2pro by increasing the distance of Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548 pairs. Furthermore, perturbation simulations finally confirmed that NSC 319990, NSC 80731, NSC 80735, NSC 67436 and NSC 37553 compounds exhibited significantly stronger binding affinity, ranging from –9.70 ± 0.61 to –11.71 ± 1.25 kcal mol–1, than that of the available inhibitor RA-0002034, ΔGFEP = − 6.45 ± 0.32 kcal mol–1. Besides, the strong correlation between ΔGFEP and Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 pair suggests that a stronger binding ligand better inhibits the biological activity of nsP2pro. Overall, these findings suggest that five NCI compounds are highly promising candidates for further experimental validation as novel nsP2pro inhibitors.Keywords: chikungunya virus, non-structural protein 2 protease, docking, free energy perturbation, molecular dynamics simulation 2.Material and methods2.1.Chikungunya virus non-structural protein 2 protease and ligand conformationsThe three-dimensional structure of CHIKV nsP2pro was downloaded from the Protein Data Bank (PDB) with PDB ID: 4ZTB) [8]. In total, 1581 trial ligands were obtained from the NCI Diversity Set VII database [33]. Moreover, the three-dimensional structure of RA-0002034 [15], an available inhibitor, of nsP2pro was downloaded from the PubChem database [34] with the corresponding ID of 139018657.2.2.Molecular docking simulationAutoDock Vina [35] with altered empirical parameters [36] was employed to preliminarily investigate the ligand binding pose and affinity to CHIKV nsP2pro. Because 4ZTB contains no native inhibitor, the Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV), an Alphavirus, nsP2pro with the PDB ID 8T8N [37] was employed to accurately characterize the CHIKV nsP2pro active site (cf. figure 1). Chain A of CHIKV nsP2pro, with sequence from 471 to 791, was selected as the docking receptor. The docking grid centre was chosen as centre of mass of the native ligand of VEEV nsP2pro after VEEV nsP2pro + its inhibitors were aligned to CHIKV nsP2pro via PyMOL tools [38]. The docking grid was selected as 20 × 20 × 20 Å, which is big enough to cover the whole of the binding site. The docking simulations were performed with an exhaustiveness value of 8, a setting statistically demonstrated to be sufficient for accurate pose prediction of standard organic ligands in comprehensive benchmarks [36,39]. Here, only one conformation with the strongest binding affinity was recorded. Figure 1.Conformation of CHIKV nsP2pro (green colour) in superposition state with VEEV nsP2pro (grey colour). In particular, the inhibitor of VEEV nsP2pro is denoted with red colour highlight.2.3.Molecular dynamics simulationGROMACS version 2023 [40] was employed to mimic two systems, including the CHIKV nsP2pro + inhibitor and the free inhibitor in solution. Particularly, nsP2pro and neutralized ions were topologized using the Amber99SB-iLDN force field [41]. Consequently, the TIP3P water model was employed to represent the water molecule [42]. The force field was used because it is the most suitable for free energy calculations [43,44]. Both systems—the nsP2pro + inhibitor and the free inhibitor—were inserted into a cubic periodic boundary condition box with a spacing of larger than 1.0 nm between system and boundary. The water molecules and neutralized ions were then inserted into the box. The number of atoms of the complex nsP2pro + inhibitor and the free inhibitor are ca 76 000 and 3660 atoms.Both systems were initially minimized using the steepest descent method. Consequently, the nsP2pro + inhibitor and free inhibitor in solution were positionally constrained in canonical and isobaric-isothermal ensemble simulations of 100 ps each. The outcome conformation was used as the original structure for 200 and 20 ns of MD simulations at 310 K, corresponding to the complexed CHIKV nsP2pro + ligand and the free ligand in solution, respectively. During MD simulations, the coordinates of the solvated systems were recorded every 100 ps. The simulation was repeated three times for each system to guarantee the sampling statistics. In particular, the MD parameters were obtained from the previous studies [45,46]. The non-bonded contact between distinct atoms was updated within 0.9 nm every 30 fs. The electrostatic (cou) and van der Waals (vdW) interactions were calculated using particle-mesh Ewald and cut-off schemes within a range of 0.9 nm, respectively. Moreover, an accurate and efficient leap-frog stochastic dynamics integrator was employed to mimic the behaviour of the solvated systems. The V-rescale thermostat and Parrinello–Rahman extended-ensemble pressure coupling were used during MD simulations.2.4.Perturbation simulationThe free energy perturbation (FEP) simulations can be used to determine the binding free energy between biomolecules with high accuracy [23,47,48]. In particular, during the simulations, the coupling parameter, λ, is used for modifying the systemic Hamiltonian. Thus, a molecule is removed from the solvated system. The difference in free energy change between the two states available, λ = 0, and removed, λ = 1, can be calculated via the Bennett's acceptance ratio approach [49]. The ligand binding free energy can be computed over perturbation simulations as the difference of free energy change in two processes including removing the inhibitor from CHIKV nsP2pro + inhibitor and the free inhibitor in solution. This approach is called the double-annihilation binding free energy method [50,51]. Moreover, in this work, the last snapshot of MD simulations was used as the initial conformation of perturbation simulations. The electrostatic coupling parameter, λcou, was selected as 0.00, 0.10, 0.20, 0.35, 0.50, 0.65, 0.80 and 1.00. Furthermore, the vdW coupling parameter, λvdW, was chosen as 0.00, 0.10, 0.25, 0.35, 0.50, 0.65, 0.75, 0.90 and 1.00. The value of the coupling parameters was chosen in line with the previous studies [23]. In addition, more details about the double-annihilation binding free energy calculations have been previously reported [23,52].2.5.Analysis toolsChemicalize, a tool of ChemAxon, was employed to estimate the inhibitor pKa [53]. A three-dimensional interaction diagram between CHIKV nsP2pro and its ligand was prepared using PLIP web application [54]. Intermolecular sidechain contact is calculated when the non-hydrogen spacing between distinct atoms is smaller than 0.45 nm. Intermolecular hydrogen bond (HB) contact is figured when two conditions are satisfied. The first condition is that the angle, ∠, between donor (D), hydrogen (H) and acceptor (A) must be larger than 135 degrees. The second condition is that the distance between D and A must be smaller than 0.35 nm. The non-hydrogen atoms root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) of the solvated system was calculated via GROMACS tools ‘gmx rms’. The distance between two atoms was computed via GROMACS tools ‘gmx mindist’. The clustering calculation was completed using ‘gmx cluster’ tools with a non-hydrogen atom cut-off of 0.3 nm. The absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion (ADME) and chemical properties of compounds were estimated via pkCSM [55]. Supplementary Material Supplementary Materials 3.Results and discussion3.1.Docking affinity and poseAs mentioned above, the CHIKV nsP2pro is one of the most favoured targets for drug design because it is associated with the viral replication [6]. In particular, the enzyme cleaves the polyproteins and unwinds the RNA. In particular, nsP2pro is a cysteine protease and it can recognize small peptide substrates. Notably, several investigations have characterized small compounds proficient of inhibiting CHIKV nsP2pro, such as RA-0002034 [15]. Besides, the structural compounds can be altered to improve their inhibitory and pharmacokinetic properties [56–58]. Therefore, screening the inhibitor for CHIKV nsP2pro from small compounds is a highly potential area of research. In this context, AutoDock Vina [35], an open-source molecular docking application, is one of the most popular protocols, with more than 28 000 citations to date. A modified version with altered empirical parameters, denoted as mVina, has a higher correlation coefficient, R = 0.62 ± 0.02, compared with the original version, R = 0.54 ± 0.02 [35,36]. The package was thus used to estimate the binding pose and affinity of 1581 NCI compounds to CHIKV nsP2pro. The distribution of the obtained molecular docking energy of these compounds to nsP2pro is shown in figure 2A. Specifically, the docking scores ranged from –4.9 to –13.3 kcal mol–1, with an average of −8.89 ± 1.42 kcal mol–1. The computed error was the standard deviation. Figure 2.(A) Distribution of molecular docking results of 1581 NCI compounds to CHIKV nsP2pro. (B) The superposition of top-lead five NCI ligands and RA-0002034 in docking state with CHIKV nsP2pro. (C) Enlarged perspective of NSC 80731 binding to CHIKV nsP2pro active site, which is obtained via molecular docking simulations. In particular, the catalytic residues were denoted as Cys478, Ser482 and His548. Red dashed lines denote Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548 pairs. (D) Interaction diagram between CHIKV nsP2pro and NSC 80731 in docking mode, which was prepared using PLIP web application [54]. (E) MD-refined binding pose of NSC 80731 to CHIKV nsP2pro and the pairs (red dashed lines) including Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548. In particular, the MD-refined structure was obtained through clustering methods. (F) Interaction diagram between CHIKV nsP2pro and NSC 80731 in MD-refined binding mode, which was prepared using PLIP web application [54].Five top-lead compounds with the strongest binding affinity to CHIKV nsP2pro are listed in table 1. Besides, RA-0002034 [15], an available inhibitor of nsP2pro, was also docked to the protease for comparison. The obtained result is also mentioned in table 1, in which the docking energy of –9.9 kcal mol–1 is in good agreement with the experimental value, ΔGEXP = −9.27 kcal mol–1. The outcomes imply that mVina is an appropriate protocol for estimating the possible binding compounds to CHIKV nsP2pro. The binding pose between ligands and nsP2pro is shown in figure 2 and figures S1–S6 in the supplementary material. The docking interaction diagrams suggested that three residues—Tyr544, Asn547 and Leu670—may act as important elements during the ligand binding process because they form HB, hydrophobic or π-stacking contacts to CHIKV nsP2pro. The ligands may indirectly alter the pairs including Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548, as they interact rigidly with the residue Asn547. It should be noted that these pairs are associated with the catalytic domain of the enzyme. Molecular docking outcome implies that five top-lead compounds may act as potential inhibitors for CHIKV nsP2pro. Table 1.The ligand binding affinity provided by molecular docking simulations.ano.ligandΔGDockΔGEXPb1NSC 319990–13.32NSC 80731–13.33NSC 80735–13.34NSC 67436–13.15NSC 37553–13.06RA-0002034 –9.9–9.27 [15]aThe unit of energy is kcal mol–1.bThe experimental binding free energy was calculated via formula ΔGEXP = RTln(Ki), where R is the gas constant, T is the absolute temperature, and Ki is the inhibition constant.3.2.Refining docking results with molecular dynamics simulationsIt should be noted that molecular docking simulations commonly use several approximations and constraints to speed up the calculation process [59–61]. The applied simplifications involved using a rigid receptor, using an implicit solvent model, incorporating a united atom model limiting a number of trail binding pose, etc. [35,60,62,63]. Therefore, although the molecular docking simulations provided an appropriate outcome, MD simulations were then carried out to refine the results. The complexes, including CHIKV nsP2pro + NCI compounds, were parametrized and mimicked using MD simulations. Besides, the CHIKV nsP2pro + RA-0002034 was also investigated because RA-0002034 acts as a positive control. The ligand binding pose and nsP2pro structure changed during MD simulations (cf. figures S1–S6 in the supplementary material). In particular, ligands have established highly optimized and stable networks of HBs and hydrophobic interactions with important active-site residues such as Tyr544, Trp549, Asn547 and Ala511. Thus the binding mechanisms were explored based on structural analyses. Each complex was simulated three times in MD simulations with a length of 200 ns. Furthermore, the free ligand in solution was mimicked for over 20 ns of MD simulations. The binding affinity of ligands to CHIKV nsP2pro was clarified using binding free energy protocols [64,65]. Here, perturbation simulations were acquired to complete this task since providing the most accurate results until the date [66,67]. Notably, this method has a proven track record of successful application across numerous biological targets [45,46,68,69,70].The CHIKV nsP2pro + ligand complexes in solution mostly reached equilibrium conditions after ca 100 ns of MD simulations according to the obtained RMSD presented in table S1 in the supplementary material. Moreover, the free ligand in solution also reached stable states after ca 2.5 ns of MD simulations (cf. supplementary material, table S2). The systemic coordinates within the equilibrium intervals were collected for structural analysis. To clarify the binding picture between nsP2pro and inhibitor, the representative conformations of the complexes in solution were estimated using the clustering method over all equilibrium snapshots. A non-hydrogen atom cut-off of 0.3 nm was applied. The ligand interaction diagrams were then investigated using PLIP web application [54]. The outcomes are described in figure 2 and figures S1–S5 in the supplementary material. MD-refined findings suggested that the residues Asn476, Ala511, Tyr512, Tyr544 and Trp549 act as crucial residues controlling the binding process of nsP2pro inhibitors. Although top-leads and the available inhibitor do not form rigid interactions to Cys478 or Ser482 or His548, the six compounds can change the pairs involving Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548 via interacting with Asn476 and Trp549. Indeed, the pairs including Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548 were significantly changed when the ligands were induced. The outcomes are described in figure 3 and table S3 in the supplementary material. In particular, the average of the spacing between Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548 is 7.4 ± 1.4 and 8.9 ± 1.8 Å, respectively, when the free nsP2pro in solution is considered. When the considered inhibitors were induced, the distances of the pair Cys478-Sγ – Nε-His548 are significantly enlarged compared to the ones of the free nsP2pro in solution and nsP2pro + RA-0002034 systems (cf. supplementary material, table S3). Meanwhile, the distance of the pair Ser482-Oγ - Nε-His548 varies depending on the specific ligand (cf. Table S3 of the Supporting Information). The findings suggest that five NCI compounds can prevent the biological activity of nsP2pro. Figure 3.Distribution of the pairs between Cys478-Sγ–Nε-His548 (upper panel) and Ser482-Oγ–Nε-His548 (lower panel). The results are obtained by analysing the MD-refined equilibrium snapshots.3.3.Perturbation simulationsThe binding free energy of ligands to CHIKV nsP2pro can be accurately estimated via FEP simulations. During simulations, the coupling parameter λ was changed to turn the system from bound to unbound states. The free energy alteration of the nsP2pro + inhibitor and free inhibitor in solution was computed using λ-alteration simulation. In particular, alchemical free energy profiles of coulomb, vdW and total terms over MD simulations are shown in figure S7 in the supplementary material. Moreover, the smooth ΔG versus λ transitions along with small computed error bars reveal excellent phase-space overlap, proving that the number of applied λ windows is sufficient (cf. supplementary material, figure S8). Furthermore, the free energy difference between two processes is calculated as the binding free energy. The obtained results are described in table 2. The binding free energy of RA-0002034 to nsP2pro via FEP calculations is ΔGFEP = −6.45 ± 0.32 kcal mol–1, which is significantly smaller than the experimental value, ΔGEXP = −9.27 kcal mol–1. The difference may be owing to the fact that only non-covalent binding free energy is taken into account in the calculations. Moreover, all five NCI compounds exhibited significantly larger binding affinities to CHIKV nsP2pro than the available inhibitor named RA-0002034. In particular, the NSC 80731 and NSC 37553 bind to nsP2pro with the strongest binding free energy of –11.71 ± 1.25 and –11.14 ± 0.32 kcal mol–1, respectively. The others including NSC 80735, NSC 67436 and NSC 319990 also unveiled a stronger binding affinity than RA-0002034 with corresponding values of –10.91 ± 2.00, –10.13 ± 0.73 and –9.70 ± 0.61 kcal mol–1, respectively. Five NCI compounds act as highly potential inhibitors as compared with the CHIKV nsP2pro.
